content_html:
Every year people ask about the night of the 15th of Sha'ban (known in Arabic as Laylat an-Nisf min Sha'ban, and in South Asia as Shab-e-Barat): does it have an established virtue, and what should be done on it? The short answer: a hadith mentions a general forgiveness for all creation on this night, except the idolater and the person who harbours enmity, and hadith scholars differ on whether it is authentic. As for special prayers and du'as for this night, none of them is established. In 1448 AH it is expected to fall on the evening of Friday 22 January 2027.

In this article we present the hadith and its grading fairly, explain which popular practices are not authentic, discuss the meaning of Allah's words ﴿فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ﴾, "Therein [i.e., on that night] is made distinct every precise matter" (Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:4, translation: Sahih International), and summarise the scholars' views on spending the night in worship. The aim is that you worship Allah on this night with clear knowledge, while keeping your affection for fellow Muslims who follow a different view.

What is the virtue of the 15th of Sha'ban night?

A hadith says: "Allah looks upon His creation on the night of the middle of Sha'ban and forgives all His creation except an idolater or one who harbours enmity." Al-Albani graded it authentic on the strength of its many chains, while most early hadith scholars graded it weak. No special prayer or specific du'a for this night is established, and the night in which matters are decreed is Laylat al-Qadr, according to the majority of Quran commentators.

The virtue mentioned in the hadith is a general forgiveness from which two kinds of people are excluded: the one who associates partners with Allah, and the mushahin, the person whose heart holds hostility and rivalry towards a fellow Muslim. The same meaning is established in Sahih Muslim for every week, as we will see. So the biggest practical lesson of this night is to cleanse the heart of shirk (associating partners with Allah) and of grudges.

When is the night of the 15th of Sha'ban 1448?

In the Islamic calendar the night comes before its day. So the night of mid-Sha'ban is the night that begins at sunset on the 14th of Sha'ban, followed by the day of the 15th. Since 1 Sha'ban 1448 AH is expected to fall on Saturday 9 January 2027 according to the Umm al-Qura calendar, the dates work out as follows:

DayHijri dateExpected Gregorian date
Start of Sha'ban1 Sha'ban 1448 AHSaturday 9 January 2027
Start of the night of mid-Sha'ban (at Maghrib)Evening of 14 Sha'banEvening of Friday 22 January 2027
The day of mid-Sha'ban15 Sha'banSaturday 23 January 2027
The White Days of Sha'ban13, 14 and 15 Sha'ban21, 22 and 23 January 2027
Start of Ramadan1 Ramadan 1448 AHAround 8 February 2027

These dates are approximate and may move a day earlier or later depending on when the Sha'ban moon is confirmed in your country. Note that this year the night of mid-Sha'ban is the night before Saturday, straight after Friday.

The hadith "Allah looks upon His creation on the night of mid-Sha'ban": text and grading

Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"Allah looks down on the night of the middle of Sha'ban and forgives all His creation, except an idolater or one who harbours enmity." (Sunan Ibn Majah 1390)

A similar narration is reported from Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) by Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, and from a number of other Companions with chains of varying strength. Hadith scholars differed in their verdict on it:

  • Those who graded it authentic through its combined chains: Shaykh al-Albani, who included it in as-Silsilah as-Sahihah (1144). He noted that none of its individual chains is free of weakness, but held that its many chains and supporting reports from several Companions strengthen one another, so he judged the text authentic.
  • Those who graded it weak: many of the early imams of hadith. Ibn Rajab al-Hanbali reported that most scholars graded the hadith on the virtue of the night of mid-Sha'ban as weak, and Abu Bakr ibn al-'Arabi is reported to have said that nothing reliable is authentic about this night.

This is a legitimate disagreement among specialists in grading chains of narration. That is why IslamQA, in discussing the issue, states that authenticating or weakening a hadith is a matter of scholarly judgement (ijtihad), in which those who differ should not be harshly criticised. Most importantly, even if the hadith is authentic, it mentions forgiveness from Allah, and it does not mention any prayer, du'a or specific act.

An authentic meaning that applies every week

What reassures the heart is that the meaning of this hadith is established without dispute in Sahih Muslim. Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported that the Prophet ﷺ said:

"The gates of Paradise are opened on Monday and Thursday, and every servant who does not associate anything with Allah is forgiven, except a man who has enmity between himself and his brother..." (Sahih Muslim 2565)

It is also established that Allah descends to the lowest heaven every night when the last third of the night remains, and says: "Who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? Who is asking of Me, that I may give him? Who is seeking My forgiveness, that I may forgive him?" (Sahih al-Bukhari 1145; Sahih Muslim 758). So the door of forgiveness and du'a is open every night, and the night of mid-Sha'ban is one of those nights.

What is not established about the night of the 15th of Sha'ban?

Many practices and hadith about this night have spread that have no basis or are extremely weak. Here are the best known:

Popular practice or textVerdictExplanation
"When it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban, spend its night in prayer and fast its day"Fabricated or extremely weakReported by Ibn Majah (1388). Its chain includes Abu Bakr ibn Abi Sabrah, about whom Ahmad and Ibn Ma'in said: he fabricated hadith
The hadith of A'ishah about the Prophet ﷺ going out to al-Baqi' on the night of mid-Sha'ban, and Allah forgiving more than the number of hairs on the sheep of the tribe of KalbWeakReported by at-Tirmidhi (739), who quoted al-Bukhari weakening it because its chain is broken; al-Albani also graded it weak
Salat al-Alfiyyah: one hundred rak'ahs, reciting Surah al-Ikhlas ten times in eachIts hadith is fabricated and the prayer is an innovation (bid'ah)An-Nawawi said in al-Majmu': the Ragha'ib prayer and the prayer of the night of mid-Sha'ban are two reprehensible innovations
Six rak'ahs after Maghrib with Surah Ya-Sin recited three times, for long life and abundant provisionNo basisNot reported in any authentic hadith, nor in any weak one worth considering; it is a later custom
A special du'a for the night recited in groups, asking for misery to be erased from the "Mother of the Book"Not established from the Prophet ﷺIt is not authentically attributed to him, and one should not believe it has a special virtue on this night
Believing that lifespans and provision are decreed on this nightContrary to the majority viewThe blessed night in Surah ad-Dukhan is Laylat al-Qadr according to the majority of commentators

The principle here is the Prophet's ﷺ saying: "Whoever introduces into this matter of ours something that is not part of it, it will be rejected." (Sahih al-Bukhari 2697; Sahih Muslim 1718). So whoever wishes to pray at night on this night should pray as they would on any other night, without an invented number of rak'ahs or a special format.

Are lifespans and provision decreed on the night of mid-Sha'ban?

Those who say so rely on Allah's words at the start of Surah ad-Dukhan:

﴿حم (١) وَالْكِتَابِ الْمُبِينِ (٢) إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مُّبَارَكَةٍ ۚ إِنَّا كُنَّا مُنذِرِينَ (٣) فِيهَا يُفْرَقُ كُلُّ أَمْرٍ حَكِيمٍ (٤)﴾

"Ha, Meem. By the clear Book, indeed, We sent it down during a blessed night. Indeed, We were to warn [mankind]. Therein [i.e., on that night] is made distinct every precise matter." (Surah Ad-Dukhan 44:1-4, translation: Sahih International)

It is reported from 'Ikrimah that this blessed night is the night of mid-Sha'ban. But the majority of commentators hold that it is Laylat al-Qadr (the Night of Decree), because the Quran explains itself:

  • The verse says the Quran was sent down on this blessed night.
  • Allah says: ﴿إِنَّا أَنزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ﴾ "Indeed, We sent it [i.e., the Qur'an] down during the Night of Decree." (Surah Al-Qadr 97:1, translation: Sahih International)
  • And Allah says: ﴿شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ الَّذِي أُنزِلَ فِيهِ الْقُرْآنُ﴾ "The month of Ramadan [is that] in which was revealed the Qur'an." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:185, translation: Sahih International)

So the blessed night in which the Quran was revealed is Laylat al-Qadr, and it is in Ramadan, not Sha'ban. This is why Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir that whoever claims it is the night of mid-Sha'ban has gone far from the mark, because the Quran states plainly that it is in Ramadan. According to the commentators, the meaning of "therein is made distinct every precise matter" is that on that night the events of the coming year, such as lifespans and provision, are set out from the Preserved Tablet to the recording angels.

You can read the explanation of these verses yourself in Tafsir al-Muyassar and Tafsir as-Sa'di, and we compare the two in our article on Tafsir as-Sa'di and Tafsir al-Muyassar.

What do scholars say about spending the night of mid-Sha'ban in worship?

This is an old disagreement among scholars, and knowing the positions helps us to be fair and avoid quarrelling. They can be summarised in three views:

ViewWho held itSummary of the evidence
It is recommended to spend the night in worshipIbn Rajab reported that a group of the Tabi'in (the generation after the Companions) in Syria, such as Khalid ibn Ma'dan and Makhul, honoured the night and strove in worship on it. Today Egypt's Dar al-Ifta holds this viewThe hadith graded authentic through its chains, and ash-Shafi'i's statement in al-Umm: "It has reached us that du'a is answered on five nights", among them the night of mid-Sha'ban
Worship on it individually, without gathering or a special formatIbn Rajab reported this from al-Awza'i. Close to it is the view of Ibn Taymiyyah: a person praying on it alone has precedent among the early Muslims, but gathering in mosques for a set prayer is an innovationCombining what is reported about its virtue with the prohibition on inventing new forms of worship
Not singling it out for any worshipIbn Rajab reported that most of the scholars of the Hijaz, such as 'Ata' and Ibn Abi Mulaykah, rejected it. Shaykh Ibn Baz held this view and considered celebrating the night an innovationIn their view the hadith are weak, and singling the night out is not reported from the Prophet ﷺ or the Companions

See the statement of Egypt's Dar al-Ifta (Arabic) for the first view, and the explanation on IslamQA for the last.

What does everyone agree on?

  • The hundred-rak'ah prayer and similar special formats have no basis.
  • Night prayer, du'a and seeking forgiveness are prescribed every night, including this one, because of the authentic hadith of Allah's descent.
  • Enmity and shirk both block forgiveness, so purifying the heart is required at all times.
  • This issue is not worth becoming a cause of disputes between Muslims; such disputes are the very "enmity" (shahna') the hadith warns against.

Is fasting on the 15th of Sha'ban prescribed?

No authentic hadith singles out the 15th of Sha'ban for fasting, and the hadith that says "and fast its day" is fabricated, as explained above. However, fasting it is legitimate for other reasons:

  • It is one of the White Days: the 13th, 14th and 15th of every Hijri month, which it is sunnah to fast every month. In Sha'ban 1448 they are expected to fall on 21, 22 and 23 January 2027. See our article on fasting the White Days.
  • Sha'ban is a month of frequent fasting: A'ishah (may Allah be pleased with her) said: "I never saw him fast more in any month than he did in Sha'ban." (Sahih al-Bukhari 1969; Sahih Muslim 1156). The details and rulings are in our article on fasting in Sha'ban.

So whoever fasts the 15th with the intention of the White Days, or as general voluntary fasting in Sha'ban, has done well, as long as they do not believe it has a special virtue that is not established.

What should I actually do on the night of mid-Sha'ban?

If you would like to make the most of this night, here are deeds with a firm basis that are prescribed on any night without dispute:

  1. Make peace with anyone you are at odds with: send a message of salam to a relative or friend you have cut off. This is the deed closest to the meaning of the hadith.
  2. Renew your tawhid and repent: seek Allah's forgiveness for your sins, and review anything that might taint your tawhid (belief in Allah's oneness), such as attachment to other than Allah.
  3. Pray what you can at night: two rak'ahs or more with witr, as you would on other nights, without a special number.
  4. Ask Allah for whatever you wish: the good of this world and the next, especially in the last third of the night, using the authentic du'as of the Quran and Sunnah.
  5. Read your daily Quran portion: and if you have not yet started, begin your preparation plan for Ramadan, as in our Ramadan Quran completion schedule.
  6. Do not share what is not authentic: check any hadith before sharing it, using the Dorar hadith encyclopedia (Arabic).

Summary: the 15th of Sha'ban between the established and the unestablished

The night of mid-Sha'ban is mentioned in a hadith about forgiveness for all creation except the idolater and the person who harbours enmity. Al-Albani graded it authentic through its combined chains, while most early scholars graded it weak, as Ibn Rajab reported. No special prayer such as the hundred rak'ahs is established for it, nor any specific du'a, and the hadith "spend its night in prayer and fast its day" is not authentic. The night in which every precise matter is made distinct is Laylat al-Qadr in Ramadan, according to the majority of commentators. Scholars are divided between those who recommend spending the night in worship, those who allow individual worship on it, and those who do not single it out, and they agree that night prayer and du'a are prescribed every night. This year it is expected on the evening of Friday 22 January 2027. Make it a chance to clear your heart and repent, and ask the scholars in your country about your own situation.

faq.q: Is the hadith about the 15th of Sha'ban authentic?
faq.a: The hadith "Allah looks down on the night of the middle of Sha'ban and forgives all His creation except an idolater or one who harbours enmity" is reported by Ibn Majah and Ibn Hibban. Al-Albani graded it authentic in as-Silsilah as-Sahihah through its combined chains, while most early scholars graded it weak, as Ibn Rajab reported. The hadith "spend its night in prayer and fast its day" is fabricated or extremely weak.

faq.q: Is there a special du'a for the night of the 15th of Sha'ban?
faq.a: No du'a specific to this night is established from the Prophet ﷺ, and the du'as circulated for it are not authentically attributed to him. You may ask Allah for whatever you wish of the good of this world and the next, as on any night, especially in the last third of the night, since it is established that Allah descends every night and answers those who call on Him.

faq.q: Is destiny written on the night of the 15th of Sha'ban?
faq.a: The majority of Quran commentators hold that the blessed night in Surah ad-Dukhan, in which every precise matter is made distinct, is Laylat al-Qadr, because Allah says He revealed the Quran on it, and that He revealed it in Ramadan and on the Night of Decree. The view that it is the night of mid-Sha'ban is reported from 'Ikrimah, and Ibn Kathir and others rejected it.

faq.q: What is the ruling on the hundred-rak'ah prayer on the 15th of Sha'ban?
faq.a: The hundred-rak'ah prayer known as al-Alfiyyah has no authentic basis; its hadith is fabricated, and an-Nawawi called it a reprehensible innovation. Whoever wants to pray on this night should pray whatever rak'ahs they can with witr, as on any other night, without a special number or format.

faq.q: When is the night of the 15th of Sha'ban 1448?
faq.a: Sha'ban 1448 AH is expected to begin on Saturday 9 January 2027, so the night of mid-Sha'ban begins at Maghrib on Friday 22 January 2027, and the 15th is Saturday 23 January. These are approximate dates according to the Umm al-Qura calendar and depend on the moon sighting in each country.
